subject: NYBridge - CAIQ / log retention sampling & keystore deletion evidence
messages:
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@nybridge.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ follow-up: log retention granularity + sample proof-of-delete request

Hi David,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. Procurement is progressing but we ran into two items in the CAIQ/SIG review that need more detail before our legal team will sign off:

1) Log retention granularity: the CAIQ answers indicate "debug and access logs retained up to 90 days by default". Can you confirm how that applies at tenant scope (per-tenant TTLs, sub-second indices, time-based partitions)? We need a plain-English description we can attach to our SOC 2 evidence package.

2) Proof-of-delete / scope-limited erasure: we have one tenant (Tenant ID: NYB-7f9c3) that needs confirmation of a targeted deletion event from last quarter (2027-03-02 to 2027-03-09). Procurement expects a sampling-based attestation or an auditable proof that logs/objects associated with that tenant were removed per the deletion request. Specifically: chain-of-custody for exported artifacts, object hashes for deleted blobs, and a signed deletion certificate.

Attached is our CAIQ extract and procurement checklist. Can you outline a deliverable set and an estimated time-to-deliver? If Redwood cannot provide object-level hashes we need to know alternative compensating controls that meet audit expectations.

Appreciate a short reply with options — procurement wants this before the end of next week.

Best,
Sara
Sara Lewis
Security & Procurement Lead
NyBridge Financial

Attachment: CAIQ_questions_NYB.xlsx
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@nybridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up: log retention granularity + sample proof-of-delete request

Sara —

Thanks for the detail, and for the attachment. Quick clarifying questions before we propose a firm plan:

• For the tenant-scoped TTL question — do you want the answer to be strictly "how our defaults behave" or show the precise config that was in use for NYB-7f9c3 during Mar 2027 (we can pull the historical config snapshot if helpful)?
• For the deletion request: was the original request a self-service erase via your console/API, or did NyBridge perform a support request with a ticket number? If there's a ticket/ref we can tie artifacts to it for chain-of-custody.

Options we can offer (high-level):
A) Targeted evidence bundle (recommended): export of log metadata for the specified time window (CSV of keys, timestamps, object-ids), keystore snapshot showing key residency and rotation records, and a signed deletion certificate referencing SHA256 hashes of final deleted artifacts. We can also provide a short attestation letter from our Security team. Estimated time: 7–10 business days after we get the tenant ID + confirmation of the deletion ticket.

B) Sampling + compensating controls: if we cannot produce object hashes (e.g., logs already compacted/obfuscated), we can run a retention-sampling exercise: snapshot index-level metadata, produce an algorithmic sampling matrix, and provide a JSON digest of the sampled objects with hash chains and an explanation of retention pipeline (batches, compaction window). Estimated time: 10–14 business days.

C) Alternative: if you need a third-party attestation, we can coordinate an on-site/remote audit session where our infra team reproduces the deletion workflow with logs and demonstrates the tombstone sweep for a representative tenant. Timing depends on audit scheduling.

I'll draft a short deliverables checklist and timeline and loop in Marissa for the SOC2/CAIQ candidate responses and Ben for the keystore/export mechanics.

—David
David Kim
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention-sampling-proposal.pdf
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@nybridge.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@nybridge.com
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up: log retention granularity + sample proof-of-delete request

David — thanks, that helps. Answers below so you can pick the appropriate path:

• Tenant ID: NYB-7f9c3 (confirmed).
• Deletion request: support ticket #NYB-20270312-erase (we submitted a formal support request on 2027-03-12 at 15:22 UTC; the support confirmation shows the action as "completed").
• Litigation hold: none. No legal hold or regulator request on the tenant.

Procurement preference is Option A (targeted evidence bundle) — they specifically want object-level hashes and a signed deletion certificate. If you can provide the keystore snapshot and signed cert that references SHA256 hashes of deleted objects we should be able to close the item.

One caveat: procurement may insist on a short chain-of-custody note explaining who accessed the export and when (ideally with human-readable timestamps and the internal ticket reference).

Can Redwood commit to the 7–10 business day estimate? If so we'll flag the contract review as green.

Thanks — I can be available for a 30-min sync if it helps.

Sara
Sara Lewis
Security & Procurement Lead
NyBridge Financial

Attachment: procurement_requirements.pdf
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@nybridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up: log retention granularity + sample proof-of-delete request

Sara —

Thanks for the tenant ID and the support ticket reference. We can commit to Option A with the following acceptance criteria and deliverables:

Deliverables (target 8 business days):
1) Export package (S3-stub archive) containing:
   - log_metadata.csv (object-id, tenant-id, object-type, timestamp, size, storage-path)
   - export_manifest.json (export start/end time, operator id, associated support ticket NYB-20270312-erase)
   - object_hashes.csv (object-id, SHA256) for objects that are recoverable from retention stores

2) Keystore residency snapshot (keystore_snapshot.txt) showing key-id mappings and rotation events during Mar 2027.

3) Signed deletion certificate (deletion_certificate.pdf) issued by Redwood Security with:
   - scoped statement referencing Tenant NYB-7f9c3 and ticket NYB-20270312-erase
   - list of object-ids and associated SHA256 hashes (where available)
   - chain-of-custody table (export operator, timestamp, export checksum)
   - contact for verification and an internal audit reference id (RWF-SEC-20270628-nyb)

4) CAIQ addendum (CAIQ_response_NYB.pdf) with an explicit plain-language explanation of tenant-level TTL behavior, compaction windows, and retention partitioning.

Notes & limitations:
• Some compacted/rolled-up debug indices may not contain object-level blobs (they are stored as compressed segments). In those cases we will provide the export_manifest and a sampling digest showing the compaction windows the object was subject to, plus hash-chains for the sampled segments (compensating control).
• We will include an audit-style chain-of-custody. The export will be checksum-signed and recorded in our internal evidence tracker.

Next steps:
• I will circulate the evidence checklist and an internal runbook to Marissa and Ben to get a firm ETA.
• Can you confirm the preferred delivery method (secure SFTP, encrypted shared Drive link, or direct HubSpot upload to your procurement portal)?
• We can set up a 30-min technical Q&A with our Security team on Thu Jul 1 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work for you?

If that all looks good I'll mark this as scoped and begin work tomorrow.

Regards,
David Kim
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence-deliverables-checklist.pdf
